issues.problem: gsplat normalises quaternions; the official diff-gaussian-rasterization does not (forward.cu/backward.cu: `glm::vec4 q = rot;// / glm::length(rot)`). Official R-VQ rotations (sum of 6 codes) and the decoded test-time rotations are therefore used un-normalised in the covariance.
issues.evidence: official render(): rotations = pc.vq_rot(...) / pc._rotation passed raw; gsplat rasterization() normalises. Effect is O(R-VQ residual error) in |q|-1, so small.
issues.fix: Document as gap G10; optionally quantify |q|-1 on a decoded checkpoint. No code change is needed unless |q| deviates by more than a few percent.

issues.where: fp32 hash grid and MLP vs tcnn fp16 (G3)
issues.problem: tcnn keeps fp32 master params but runs the grid and MLP in fp16 (`params.to(half)`, loss_scale 128, fp16 param grads). Here everything is fp32. With Adam eps=1e-15, fp16 gradient underflow in tcnn zeroes dust gradients that fp32 turns into full-lr steps. This can change the hash-value distribution (|theta|>0.1 pruning, Huffman size) and PSNR slightly. The gap is listed but not bounded.
issues.fix: If the benchmark misses the PP storage (hash 7.4 MB target) or PSNR, emulate it cheaply: cast features and params through half in forward and flush grads via (g*128).half()/128 before Adam. Report hash-pruned fraction vs the paper.

issues.problem: `test_equals_validation` is not evidence of ss-eval fidelity. Validation at step 30000 already runs the baked render_decoded path, so both numbers use the same code. The real guard is the bake_eval probe (fresh bank-free render == baked render; baked feature == bank.features(dec['means'], dec['hash'])). That check holds by construction: positions are frozen and fp16-rounded, and the contraction is the same fp32 function. It is correct, but the probe never compares the live-bank render with decoded weights against the baked render.
issues.evidence: Official precompute(): contract(xyz.half()) then recolor(...). Plugin bake: bank.features(dec['means'], dec['hash']) with dec['means'] fp16->fp32. Identical inputs, so ss-eval == querying the decoded grid at render time.
issues.fix: Optional extra probe: set bank.hash.params to dec['hash'] and bank.mlp to dec['mlp'] (live path, no mask/R-VQ) and assert equality with the baked render.

issues.problem: The runtime applies the per-Gaussian Adam step at step 30000 before the final prune/encode (official skips every optimizer step there). The displacement is at most lr_final*extent (1.6e-6*extent) per parameter; it is mostly erased by fp16 rounding of xyz. Negligible.
issues.evidence: train.py: `if iteration < opt.iterations: optimizer.step()`; runtime.py steps all optimizers unconditionally.

summary: No critical or major issues. The volume mask (STE on scale and opacity, eps 0.01, lambda 5e-4, mask lr 0.01, init 1.0, prune at 500<it<15000 every 100 and every 1000 from 15000, final prune) matches the official code. The hash grid matches tcnn (16x2, 2^19, base 16, scale 1.447; level table, hashing and SH-at-(2d-1) verified against source/tcnn), and positions are contracted and detached as in the official render. The MLP matches (2x64 ReLU, no bias, 8192 padded params; net Adam lr 0.01 eps 1e-15, closed-form ChainedScheduler, no step at 30000). R-VQ matches (6x64, last 1000 steps, 1-iter K-means, in-place Adam 1e-4, L-fold STE). Encode/decode/replace and the storage formulas match final_prune. ss-eval renders the decoded model exactly: baked features are hash(contract(fp16 xyz)) from the decoded 8-bit pruned table, as in precompute(). Residual risks are the unbounded fp16-vs-fp32 tcnn difference and the unnormalised quaternions in the official rasterizer, both minor.
